schemaNotes: Collection of externally observed outcomes for the four canonical murmur backlash cases. Every value carries the public source it was read from and the retrieval date. No value in this file was produced by the murmur engine.
outrage-proxy                  -> interval [min,max] on a 0..1 index; INPUT to the hazard fit, never scored.
affected-user-churn-share      -> interval or point; TARGET: share of affected users who left the vendor within ~1 year.
migration-destination-share:<Name> -> interval or point; TARGET: share of movers (conditional on leaving) choosing that destination. <Name> must match caseMetadata.destinations[].name.
all other metrics              -> context only; never scored by the fit.
interval:true marks value as [min,max]. Intervals encode honest uncertainty from qualitative evidence; the fit scores a prediction by clamping it into the interval.

confidence: high = primary source read directly (vendor blog, foundation press release, SEC filing, GitHub API/Wayback capture); medium = reputable trade press or official page verified via search snippet; low = secondary/aggregated or derived estimate.

Docker Hub case: no quantitative org-attrition or destination-share source exists as of 2026-11-01 (verified by search). No migration-destination-share records are encoded for it; the case therefore contributes no migration-fit targets.

caseMetadata.announcementTitle: Unity plan pricing and packaging updates (Runtime Fee: $0.20/install above revenue+install thresholds)

walkback.summary: Runtime Fee canceled entirely, effective immediately; seat prices raised instead. Partial walkback had already removed the fee for Unity Personal on 2023-09-22 (open letter).

destinations.name: Godot Engine
destinations.featureNotes: MIT-licensed, foundation-governed (Software Freedom Conservancy / Godot Foundation); strong 2D, weaker 3D/AAA tooling vs Unity; GDScript/C# retrain and export-pipeline rebuild required.

destinations.name: Unreal Engine
destinations.featureNotes: Source-available (not foundation OSS), AAA-grade parity, royalty terms; C++/Blueprint retrain.

destinations.name: Custom/In-House Engine
destinations.featureNotes: Maximum control, maximum cost; only viable for well-funded studios.

caseMetadata.notes: Destination features are model inputs assigned by the calibrator from public product facts; they are observations of nothing.

caseMetadata.announcementTitle: HashiCorp adopts Business Source License (MPL 2.0 -> BSL 1.1 on all future releases)

destinations.name: OpenTofu
destinations.featureNotes: Terraform fork under Linux Foundation; MPL 2.0; drop-in for Terraform 1.5.x state and config.

destinations.name: Pulumi
destinations.featureNotes: Apache-2.0 IaC with general-purpose languages; different paradigm, full rewrite of modules.

destinations.name: HCP Terraform (managed)
destinations.featureNotes: Vendor's own managed offering: full parity, commercial contract; a managed-cloud commitment rather than an exit.

caseMetadata.notes: Terraform remained the market-dominant IaC tool after the license change; the fork is the quantitatively documented exit path.

caseMetadata.announcementTitle: Redis adopts dual source-available licensing (BSD-3 -> RSALv2/SSPLv1 from Redis 7.4)

destinations.name: Valkey
destinations.featureNotes: BSD-3 fork under Linux Foundation, announced 2024-03-28; drop-in replacement; hyperscaler-backed; made a managed default at AWS and Google Cloud.

destinations.name: Dragonfly
destinations.featureNotes: Redis-API-compatible multi-threaded store; BSL 1.1 licensed during the decision window (relicensed Apache-2.0 later); different architecture, partial command coverage.

destinations.name: KeyDB
destinations.featureNotes: BSD-3 Redis-compatible fork; acquired by Snapchat (2022), development largely stagnant by 2024.

caseMetadata.notes: Redis Inc. kept growing after the pivot (ARR figures in records), so the observed mover pool is small relative to the install base; conditional destination shares are measured mainly by Valkey's hyperscaler defaults.

caseMetadata.announcementTitle: Docker communicates intent to sunset Free Team organizations (email to orgs; deletion threat with 30-day window)

walkback.summary: Docker's own FAQ records the reversal: intent communicated 2023-03-14, reversed 2023-03-24; no organizations were deleted and the paid-upgrade threat was withdrawn.

destinations.name: GitHub Packages (ghcr.io)
destinations.featureNotes: Context only — this case contributes no migration-fit targets (see schemaNotes).

caseMetadata.notes: The announcement itself was an email reproduced across community forums rather than a single canonical blog URL; the official FAQ page (cited) states both the 2023-03-14 intent and the 2023-03-24 reversal.

cases.notes: Interval anchored by: CEO departure 27 days after announcement (Verge, 2023-10-09); documented ads boycott by 16 studios within days (mobilegamer.biz report); partial walkback within 10 days; full cancellation at 365 days. No walkback has ever been faster in the corpus.

No direct measurement of Unity churn exists. Bounds reasoned from: Unity retained its dominant engine position and later raised seat prices (official pricing page); the fee was fully canceled within a year, defusing the driver; documented departures exist but are individually notable (e.g. Mega Crit moving Slay the Spire 2 to Godot) rather than a mass exodus. Treat as an honest interval, not a measurement.

Godot is the dominant publicly stated destination for leavers. Supporting aggregate: Godot repo 75.2k stars on 2023-09-30 (Wayback capture, 18 days post-announcement) growing to 111,357 stars by 2026-11-01 (GitHub API). Interval is a structured estimate from switch statements and destination growth; no survey of Unity churners exists.
Unreal is the high-parity commercial alternative; press coverage of the reaction period lists it as the second stated destination. Structured estimate, LOW confidence.
Residual destination with no quantitative source; wide interval, LOW confidence.
Wayback Machine capture of the GitHub repo page dated 2023-09-30, i.e. 18 days after the announcement: 75.2k stars, 14.7k forks.
GitHub REST API stargazers_count read 2026-11-01. Growth vs the 2023-09-30 capture: +36,157 stars in ~3.1 years, with the steepest documented surge in Sep-Oct 2023.
mobilegamer.biz tracking, late Sep 2023: 16 studios had switched off Unity Ads/ironSource SDKs pending policy change. The corpus timeline's 'over 500 studios' is NOT supported by any located source.
Announcement 2023-09-12 -> retirement effective immediately 2023-10-09.
2023-09-12 -> 2024-09-12, 'cancel the Runtime Fee, effective immediately'. Editor terms updated 2024-10-10 to remove Runtime Fee language (unity.com/products/pricing-updates).
SEC 10-K confirms 'approximately 25% of our workforce' (Jan 2024 company reset). Context only: a company reset, not evidence of customer churn.

Anchors: an organized fork with formal pledges from 140+ organizations and 600+ individuals formed within 41 days; no walkback, no executive departure; HashiCorp's commercial trajectory stayed intact. High but not terminal outrage.

OpenTofu reached roughly 10-15% adoption among IaC practitioners by 2026 from a zero baseline (LOW-confidence secondary estimate), while Terraform remained dominant. Not all OpenTofu adoption is BSL-motivated churn; bounds are the honest span of that evidence.

OpenTofu is the only drop-in community fork (state-compatible, MPL 2.0, Linux Foundation governance, 18+ committed full-time developers). Movers who stayed in the HCL ecosystem overwhelmingly landed there.
Paradigm switch (general-purpose languages); no quantitative share source. Structured estimate.

Committing to the vendor's managed cloud was explicitly unaffected by BSL ('Customers of enterprise and cloud-managed HashiCorp products will see no change'). No quantitative share source; structured estimate.
Linux Foundation press release, 2023-09-20: 'formal pledges spanning 140+ organizations and 600+ individuals', including Harness, Gruntwork, Spacelift, env0, Scalr.
Same press release.
'a starting commitment of a minimum of 18 full-time developers over at least the next five years'.
BSL announcement 2023-08-10 -> Linux Foundation launch 2023-09-20 (OpenTF manifesto campaign began in between).

Secondary estimate ('approximately 12% adoption among IaC practitioners, with 27% of teams planning to evaluate or expand'), Apr 2026. No official OpenTofu survey was located as of retrieval; treat as directional.

Anchors: a Linux Foundation fork uniting AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle, Ericsson and Snap formed in under a week after the announcement (per AWS's own retrospective); no walkback; distributions planned removals.

Redis Inc. passed $300M ARR in Jan 2026, up from ~$200M in 2023 (Sacra secondary estimate, LOW), i.e. the paying base grew through the licensing change; the moving minority is bounded by Valkey's managed-service uptake. Upper bound generous for managed-service migration that is only partially attributable to the license change.

Valkey became the default exit: AWS ElastiCache/MemoryDB support (2024-10-08) with Valkey priced 20-33% below Redis OSS equivalents, Google Memorystore Valkey 8.0 (2024-10-03), Linux Foundation governance, drop-in compatibility. Structured interval; hyperscaler defaults are the dominant observable.
API-compatible alternative but BSL-licensed during the decision window and architecturally divergent; no quantitative share source. Structured estimate.
Development largely stagnant post-acquisition; no quantitative share source; structured estimate of a marginal destination.
AWS database blog, 2024-10-08: 'over 500K container pulls, thousands of contributions, and support from 40+ companies... in the last six months'.
Same AWS blog: 'support from 40+ companies'.
2024-03-20 -> 2024-10-08 GA of Valkey 7.2 on ElastiCache and MemoryDB; ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey priced 33% below Redis OSS, node-based 20% below; MemoryDB for Valkey 30% below.
2024-03-20 -> 2024-10-03 (Valkey 8.0 on Memorystore); general availability 2025-04-18 (414 days).
Trade press, 2026-01-27. Stay-side evidence: the paying customer base grew through the license change.
Secondary private-company estimate (Sacra) as surfaced in search results on 2026-11-01; not directly fetched. Baseline for the $300M comparison only.

Anchors: the fastest and most complete walkback in the corpus (full reversal in 10 days, no deletions executed); immediate viral coverage across developer forums (osnews 2023-03-15 and community threads). Docker's own FAQ records both dates.

Weakest target in the corpus, explicitly flagged: NO quantitative org-attrition source exists as of 2026-11-01. Bounds reasoned from the full 10-day reversal (the deletion driver was removed before it executed) and Docker Hub's continued role as the default registry; wide interval on purpose. Individual org moves to ghcr.io/ECR are documented anecdotally in forum threads only.
Docker's own FAQ: 'Docker communicated its intent to sunset the Docker Free Team plan on March 14, 2023, but this decision was reversed on March 24, 2023.'
Reaction-scale marker: widespread trade and community coverage within 24h of the email (osnews 2023-03-15; devtalk and Reddit threads same week). Encoded as presence, not a count.
